state.lastRunNotes: Broad macro selloff continues to accelerate (STW -4.7% today): rising bond yields ahead of the RBA's Sep 28-29 meeting (all four majors now forecasting a hike) plus AI-disruption fears for software are compressing growth-stock multiples market-wide, with volume still well below average (vol_x 0.03-0.78) confirming no capitulation, just a broad derating. None of my three held positions have company-specific bad news: CBA is down on rate-hike-driven sector pressure not NSW contract concerns, PME (-16% today) has zero negative company news and remains above its A$150 stop, and TLS is actually up 1.4%. Growth/core split excluding cash is ~37%/63%, within the 35-65% band, and cash is 61% of NAV. Holding across the board - no genuine stock-specific catalyst to trade on.
